summary: Causal grouped-query prompt attention on BF16 tensor cores with an online softmax, keeping scores in registers instead of a score matrix in memory
implementation_scope: CUDA kernel for head dimensions 64, 128 and 256 over a contiguous BF16 KV cache: 64 queries per block, 32-key tiles, ldmatrix with a 16-byte XOR swizzle, cp.async double buffering, online softmax with BF16 probabilities, causal chunk offsets and grouped-query heads; a host reference of the direct and the tiled online-softmax attention. Paged or quantized caches and the surrounding projections are engine supplied.

agent_guidance.use_when: Prompt chunks attend over a long context and the score matrix of the straightforward formulation dominates attention time or memory
agent_guidance.avoid_when: Prompts are short (the score matrix is small), the step is decode with one query per head, or the cache layout is paged or quantized without an adapted load
provides: Online softmax over key tiles with a running row maximum and sum, never holding a full score row
S = Q K^T and O = P V on BF16 tensor cores with register reuse of the score accumulators as the P fragment
Row sums over the same BF16-rounded probabilities that feed P V
Conflict-free ldmatrix through a 16-byte XOR swizzle and cp.async K/V double buffering
Causal chunk offsets (query pos0 + t sees keys through pos0 + t) and grouped-query head mapping
A host reference showing the tiled evaluation equals the direct definition, with optional probability rounding
engine_supplies: Queries after normalization and rotary embedding, and the chunk's keys and values written to the cache first
Paged or quantized cache access, if its cache is not contiguous BF16
The output gate or projection after attention
Whole-model quality measurement of the BF16 probability rounding
preserve: The causal rule and the grouping of query heads onto key/value heads
Normalization by a row sum of exactly the probability values used in P V
A fully masked tile leaves a row's maximum, sum and output unchanged
adapt: Query and key tile sizes, pipeline stages and supported head dimensions
The probability format and its error
Sharing one K/V tile across a group's query heads, and paged or quantized cache loads

code_files.purpose: Flash-style BF16 tensor-core causal attention kernel for head dimensions 64, 128 and 256
Host direct and tiled online-softmax attention with optional probability rounding

requires.hardware: CUDA C++17+ on sm_80+ (BF16 mma.sync, ldmatrix, cp.async); Python 3.11+ standard library for the reference
requires.model: Softmax attention with grouped-query (or multi-head) key/value heads and a contiguous BF16 KV cache
requires.workload: Prompt chunks at long context, single request or one chunk at a time

contract.input: BF16 queries [T][q_stride], BF16 key and value caches [pos0 + T][kv_stride], T, pos0, head counts, head dimension and score scale
contract.output: FP32 attention output [T][out_stride] per query head
contract.ownership: The engine owns queries, caches and output; the launch borrows them on the caller stream
contract.failure: Null buffers, non-positive sizes, heads not a multiple of key/value heads, unaligned or short strides and unsupported head dimensions return cudaErrorInvalidValue; launch errors are returned
contract.core_boundary: No Core change; the kernel runs inside the engine's prompt forward pass

dependencies: Python standard library for the reference

validation.host: Tiled online softmax equal to the direct definition within 1e-12; BF16 probabilities within 1e-2; short caches rejected
validation.native: CUDA kernel against an FP64 softmax reference for head dimensions 64/128/256, grouped and ungrouped heads, single-token, multi-tile and later chunks: at most 1.3e-3 of the output magnitude on sm_120
validation.performance: One measured engine: 148 -> 86 ms per 2,048-token chunk at 12K context (head dimension 256, 24 query and 4 key/value heads) against a score-matrix path on an sm_120 device; no claim for other shapes
